cands.name: Clyde Chambliss, Jr.

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Civil engineer and principal of Chambliss Engineering in Prattville. Served three terms on the Autauga County Commission (1996 onward, chairman 2000-2008). Alabama State Senator for District 30 since November 2014. Listed on his campaign site as Senate Majority Floor Leader.
cands.gaps: We could not read any roll-call-backed deeds, so nothing is shown on how he voted on data centers, property taxes, land buying, growth, immigration, guns, abortion or school choice. His birthplace and the year he may have moved to Alabama are not stated in the pages we had. The education section of his campaign issues page was cut off, so his stated views on school choice and teacher pay are unknown. We found no stated position from him on data centers or on development limits, and no controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements in the sources available. Ballotpedia reports that he did not complete its 2026 candidate survey.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says his family has lived in Autauga and Elmore Counties for almost 200 years, that he is a sixth-generation Autauga Countian who was raised there, and that he has lived and worked in Senate District 30 since finishing college in 1992; no birthplace is given. · Money: 4% of money from District 30 ZIP codes after leaving out land and development money (5% before)

indep.label: 99% of all money behind them is big money
parts: 99% of campaign money from businesses, PACs or party

land.label: 7% of money from land, development, data-center, mining or utility interests

qual.background: Has served in the Alabama Senate since 2014, including the Finance and Taxation General Fund committee and the Majority Floor Leader post. Earlier he served three terms on the Autauga County Commission (chairman 2000-2008) and works as a civil engineer who owns Chambliss Engineering.
qual.why: Twelve years of legislative service, a chamber leadership post and budget-committee work, plus county elected office and business ownership, fit the top of the rubric for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: Twelve years of legislative service, a chamber leadership post and budget-committee work, plus county elected office and business ownership, fit the top of the rubric for writing law and the state budget.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he spearheaded the successful movement to protect the lives of over 6,000 unborn children a year in Alabama, and that he has consistently supported legislation to preserve Christian values. This is a campaign claim; no bill or roll call was read to confirm it.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site calls him a staunch supporter of law enforcement officers. It says that through his budget committee assignments he has made fair compensation for law enforcement and correctional officers and hiring more officers and state troopers priorities in the General Fund Budget.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised
